hypothesis: Within the ATR>30 universe, DTE-based rules (drop DTE=5 weakest bucket; size up DTE=1 strongest bucket) improve risk-adjusted returns.

FINDING-1.title: Drop DTE=5 HURTS vs baseline (-37.8pp) despite DTE=5 being the weakest avg P&L bucket
FINDING-1.detail: DTE=5 contributed total +₹7,545 (47 trades, avg +₹161). Removing them lowers total return despite the low average because they are slightly net-positive. The weak avg P&L is partly due to July's DTE=5 avg +₹1,013 (6 trades) being offset by losing months (Feb avg -₹450, May avg -₹84, Jun avg -₹87).
FINDING-1.implication: Average P&L of a DTE bucket does NOT justify filtering it out if it's net-positive. More data needed to establish whether DTE=5 is structurally weak.

FINDING-2.title: DTE=1 sizing 2x improves returns (+258pp) but is concentrated in Feb+Mar high-ATR regime
FINDING-2.detail: DTE=1 outperforms other DTE buckets in 4/6 months (+Feb, +Mar, +May, +Jul) but underperforms in Apr (-338 avg) and Jun (-420 avg). Boost adds +₹47,595 in Feb+Mar alone vs -₹4,635 in Apr+Jun. In sustained low-volatility months (Jun avg ATR ~24, Apr ~26), DTE=1 options decay too fast relative to spot movement.
FINDING-2.implication: DTE=1 outperformance is REGIME-CONDITIONAL, not structural. It works in sustained high-ATR environments but fails in moderate-ATR periods — the same market condition ATR>30 filter was meant to select.

FINDING-3.title: All DTE effects trace back to ATR regime, not DTE per se
FINDING-3.detail: When ATR is high throughout the week (Feb: 26pts, Mar: 37pts), DTE=1 options have explosive gamma. When ATR normalizes by mid-week even if it spiked at entry, DTE=1 trades fail (Apr, Jun). The 10-bar ATR entry filter doesn't guarantee that volatility persists to expiry — that requires a regime-level (multi-day) ATR signal, not a bar-level one.
FINDING-3.implication: The real missing feature is SUSTAINED ATR or a weekly ATR regime indicator. Bar-level ATR>30 correctly admits trades only when volatility is currently high but does not guarantee it stays elevated for the full DTE=1 hold.

conclusion: HYPOTHESIS REJECTED. Neither DTE=5 filtering nor DTE=1 sizing adds reliable value on top of the ATR>30 filter with 6 months of data. Both rules are dominated by the Feb+Mar high-vol regime. The ATR>30 filter remains the single validated signal. CRITICAL DATA GAP: All current research rests on one 6-month window containing one clear high-vol regime (March). Every incremental rule tested beyond ATR>30 shows regime-specific, not structural, behavior. Further experimentation on this dataset risks layer-by-layer in-sample fitting. The highest-priority action is DATA-001: acquire 2023-2025 historical NIFTY 5-min data to test ATR>30 filter across multiple regime cycles.

priority_next_action.rationale: All findings beyond ATR>30 are single-regime artifacts. Adding more rules on 6 months of data is overfitting. Only more data can determine which findings are structural.
